sections.title: Introduction

summary.text: Introduces the manual as a concise, practical primer on developing health management information systems (HMIS) for readers without time for in-depth study. It describes the intended users and explains that the closing examples show how indicators and data flows can be presented rather than prescribing a model.

sections.extract: This Manual is designed to be a quick-and-easy, user-friendly reference for the development of health management information systems (HMIS), with the focus on applications. It serves as a primer on HMIS development and provides a general overview of the basic principles, as well as the fundamental steps and issues involved in the different activities to be undertaken. The information is presented in a concise,

sections.title: The basic concepts

summary.text: Defines key terms such as information system and HMIS and lists the ten steps for developing an HMIS, from reviewing the existing system to enhancing it.

sections.extract: System A collection of components that work together to achieve a common objective1 Information System A system that provides information support to the decision-making process at each level of an organization2 Health Information System A system that integrates data collection, processing, reporting, and use of the information necessary for improving health service effectiveness and efficiency through better

sections.title: Reviewing the existing system

summary.text: Sets out the steps for reviewing an existing HMIS, including inventorying forms, assessing data quality and identifying problems in other components. It advises building on existing strengths rather than discarding systems, and the extracted text runs into steps for defining indicators. The page layout has been flattened, so headings appear broken up.

sections.extract: T E P S P R I N C I P L E (1) Make an inventory of the forms, log books and other tools used to record and summarize data at different levels. (2) Assess the quality of the data being collected using the existing forms at different levels. Among the aspects to be included in the assessment are: ➤Accuracy ➤Completeness ➤Adequacy ➤Timeliness (3) Determine the problems encountered with the current system of data

sections.title: Defining data needs

summary.text: Covers defining data needs, matching information functions to administrative levels from village to national. It lists common issues, such as poorly defined roles and staff difficulty identifying indicators, and steps for finding data sources for indicators. It advises keeping detailed data at the source and limiting reporting to higher levels.

(2) Defining minimum basic data needs. (3) Differentiating data that should be included in the routine data

sections.title: Determining the data flow

summary.text: Discusses determining HMIS data flow, listing issues such as limited capacity at lower levels to summarize data and problems storing or retrieving raw data. It recommends drawing a flow chart of information from peripheral to national level. The text also runs into steps for drafting, pretesting and revising new forms and their instruction manual.

(2) Inability to distinguish which data are needed for service delivery and which data are needed for programme management and monitoring. (3) Inability of lower administrative levels to generate summaries of raw data collected due to: ➤Lack of technical expertise of staff ➤Lack of data processing facilities

sections.title: Designing the data collection and reporting tools

summary.text: Gives principles for designing simple, short data collection and reporting tools suited to staff capability, with a sample worksheet defining a fully immunized child. It also touches on planning a pretest and specifying software requirements for reports, quality checks and analysis.

sections.extract: data collection and reporting tools P R I N C I P L E S S T E P S T he capability of the staff who will be tasked with filling out the forms must be taken into consideration in designing them. T he most effective data collection and reporting tools are simple and short. (1) Technical expertise/capability of data providers at data source is not consistent with the level of complexity needed for data collection tools

sections.title: Developing procedures for data processing

summary.text: Sets out steps for HMIS data processing, which should match the objectives of data collection and analysis, including developing or adapting software and pretesting it for bugs and usability. The text then moves into designing training based on a needs assessment. It names the elements to define for training: target group, content, strategies and duration.

sections.extract: procedures for data processing P R I N C I P L E S T E P S T he way the HMIS data is processed should be consistent with the objectives for data collection and the plans for data analysis and utilization. (4) Develop the software needed to process the data at each level where computers will be used, based on the required specifications. It may also be possible that the softwares designed to generate outputs similar

sections.title: Developing the training programme

summary.text: Describes developing HMIS training programmes suited to each target group, with a syllabus as output. It covers preparing and reproducing training materials such as a data dictionary and manuals for data providers and users, and planning evaluation in advance. A sample session plan for an introductory health statistics course is included.

sections.extract: training programme P R I N C I P L E S T E P S T raining programmes should be designed according to the needs and level of the target groups. The output of this step is a course syllabus for each training programme to be conducted. (3) Develop the training materials. sections.title: Pre-testing the system

summary.text: Explains how to plan a pretest of the HMIS by deciding where, who, what and how, including criteria for selecting sites. The text then lists steps for monitoring and evaluation, from prioritizing activities to documenting results and making recommendations.

sections.extract: following questions: (1.1) Where? Selection of the place(s) where the pre-testing will be conducted. There is a need to develop criteria for selecting the pre-testing sites. sections.title: Monitoring and evaluating the system

summary.text: Covers monitoring and evaluating the HMIS, stressing that the aim is to find what works as well as what went wrong. It names issues such as institutionalizing evaluation and finding expertise, and gives a worksheet of variables to assess, including data quality, use, computing and training. The text then moves to planning HMIS expansion and resourcing, describing HMIS development as continuous improvement.

sections.extract: and evaluating the system P R I N C I P L E S T E P S T he goal of monitoring and evaluation is not to focus on what is wrong and condemn it; rather, it is to highlight the positive aspects of the system that make it work, as well as to identify what went wrong as a basis for improving the system. sections.title: Enhancing the HMIS

summary.text: Lists steps for enhancing an HMIS, such as prioritizing options, scheduling and monitoring new components, and issues such as sustaining stakeholder interest and coordinating donors to avoid duplicate forms. It ends with a sample budget and two-year timetable showing costs and funding sources.

sections.title: Examples

summary.text: Introduces two examples, a list of indicators with data sources, collection methods and frequency, and a flow chart of the HMIS of a hypothetical country. It explains that both show how to present such information rather than prescribing content. The latter part of the extracted text is garbled symbols, apparently from the flow chart.

sections.extract: Example 1 is a list of basic indicators that might be used in Ministry of Health programmes, together with the corresponding data sources, modes and frequency of data collection, as well as the lowest administrative level where the indicator is computed. narratives.en: Figure 5.1, printed rotated, is a flow chart of EPI data from the village to the national level. Boxes for each administrative level are linked by arrows: Village Health Centre (Public Health Nurse in charge of the EPI Programme) → Statistics Unit of the District Health Service (EPI District Nurse Supervisor) → Statistics Unit of the Provincial Health Service (EPI Provincial Nurse Supervisor) → MCH Division of the Ministry of Health (MCH Programme Officer) → Planning and Statistics Office of the Ministry of Health (Information Officer).
narratives.ar: الشكل 5.1، المطبوع بشكل مُدار، مخطط انسيابي لبيانات البرنامج الموسّع للتمنيع من مستوى القرية إلى المستوى الوطني. ترتبط مربعات كل مستوى إداري بأسهم: المركز الصحي القروي (ممرضة الصحة العمومية المسؤولة عن البرنامج الموسّع للتمنيع) ← وحدة الإحصاء في الخدمة الصحية للمنطقة (مشرفة تمريض البرنامج في المنطقة) ← وحدة الإحصاء في الخدمة الصحية للإقليم (مشرفة تمريض البرنامج في الإقليم) ← شعبة صحة الأم والطفل في وزارة الصحة (موظف برنامج صحة الأم والطفل) ← مكتب التخطيط والإحصاء في وزارة الصحة (موظف المعلومات).
narratives.zh: 图5.1（旋转印刷）是扩大免疫规划数据从村级到国家级的流程图。各行政级别的方框由箭头相连：村卫生中心（负责扩大免疫规划的公共卫生护士）→ 区卫生服务统计组（扩大免疫规划区护士督导员）→ 省卫生服务统计组（扩大免疫规划省护士督导员）→ 卫生部妇幼保健司（妇幼保健规划官员）→ 卫生部规划和统计办公室（信息官员）。
narratives.es: La figura 5.1, impresa en posición girada, es un diagrama de flujo de los datos del PAI desde la aldea hasta el nivel nacional. Los recuadros de cada nivel administrativo están unidos por flechas: centro de salud de la aldea (enfermera de salud pública a cargo del PAI) → unidad de estadística del servicio de salud del distrito (enfermera supervisora del PAI de distrito) → unidad de estadística del servicio de salud provincial (enfermera supervisora del PAI provincial) → división de salud maternoinfantil del Ministerio de Salud (oficial del programa de SMI) → oficina de planificación y estadística del Ministerio de Salud (oficial de información).
narratives.fr: La figure 5.1, imprimée en rotation, est un organigramme du flux des données du PEV du village au niveau national. Les cases de chaque niveau administratif sont reliées par des flèches : centre de santé du village (infirmière de santé publique responsable du PEV) → unité de statistique du service de santé du district (infirmière superviseure PEV du district) → unité de statistique du service de santé provincial (infirmière superviseure PEV provinciale) → division de la santé maternelle et infantile du ministère de la Santé (responsable du programme SMI) → bureau de la planification et des statistiques du ministère de la Santé (chargé de l’information).
narratives.ru: Рисунок 5.1, напечатанный в повёрнутом виде, — блок-схема движения данных РПИ от уровня деревни до национального уровня. Блоки каждого административного уровня соединены стрелками: деревенский медицинский центр (медсестра общественного здравоохранения, отвечающая за РПИ) → статистическое подразделение районной службы здравоохранения (районная медсестра-супервайзер РПИ) → статистическое подразделение провинциальной службы здравоохранения (провинциальная медсестра-супервайзер РПИ) → отдел охраны здоровья матери и ребёнка Министерства здравоохранения (специалист программы ОЗМР) → отдел планирования и статистики Министерства здравоохранения (специалист по информации).

narratives.en: Monochrome photograph of a workshop: a man stands holding papers and presents beside a projection screen, while participants seated at a table listen; a banner behind reads “Tổ chức Y tế Thế giới WHO” and “Hội thảo”, and flip-chart sheets are pinned to the wall.
